title: etw: support sniffing unecrypted SMB/LDAP/WinHTTP on Windows
description:
This PR introduces logic for some ETW providers with especially nice properties. It introduces the concept of "scenarios" in etwdump which mimics some the features the (now defunct) "Microsoft Message Analyzer" had.

Basically it allows to:
- sniff unencrypted SMB (client/server) traffic
- sniff unencrypted WinINet traffic
- sniff unencrypted LDAP traffic

This is pretty useful for debugging Windows Servers. There are still more providers too implement (e.g. unencrypted IPSEC) in future work.

I also cleaned up how packets are built in `etl.c` by splitting the massive `wtap_etl_record_buffer_init` into several smaller functions that build a "context" before just calling the "build" function on it. This was necessary to support the different scenarios without making the function even bigger.

### Demos

- **SMB client (also works with server-side)**: see unencrypted traffic

![SMBClient-demo](/uploads/f904672ee2602a69d08adb4b26910b10/SMBClient-demo.mp4)

- **WinHTTP client**: see unencrypted HTTPS from the Windows Store

![WinHTTP-demo](/uploads/cf7425413b6202e25f551ef9a95c4ff9/WinHTTP-demo.mp4)

- **LDAP client**: see unencrypted SASL traffic without the secrets

(Note: requires to add a registry key for the process you're debugging, as [explained in the doc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/troubleshoot/troubleshoot-ldap-using-etw))

![LDAP-demo](/uploads/c6182b5090aa15ec70e80218d6e7e0fc/LDAP-demo.mp4)

### Notes

- As you can see in the demos, I have not figured out how to make reassembly work on HTTP :/ I tried a bunch of things, like setting a fake `tcpinfo`. For a future PR, I'd be happy if someone had guidance on how to improve this.
- Also the classic "LDAP" color doesn't appear, I don't understand why it stays white.
- Microsoft-Windows-SMBServer raw output looks wrong when packets are fragmented. I think there's a bug in Windows, because even "Microsoft Message Analyzer" show the weird broken output. The same event and defragmentation works perfectly fine for the client part :/

![image](/uploads/0b149a8ede02438c686706abf9b58274/image.png){width=400}
